overall_summary: Bitcoin sits near four-month lows after heavy liquidations and almost two billion in ETF outflows, with hot PPI, yields above five percent, and a strong dollar keeping December hike odds elevated. Extreme fear and a brief short-squeeze bounce show the market is washed out, yet fresh geopolitical strikes and liquidity drain from the Anthropic IPO add pressure. Key retail sales and FOMC minutes still loom, so the tape remains fragile for crypto.
key_points: Spot ETFs see $1.91B outflows in seven days
December hike nearly certain, 50bp odds rising
Fear at extreme 10; geo strikes add risk-off

items.title: Bitcoin Hits Four-Month Low Near $62K on $2B Liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin slumped to as low as about sixty-two thousand dollars over the weekend, its weakest level since July, before bouncing back toward the mid-sixty-fours. Roughly two billion dollars in crypto positions were liquidated in twenty-four hours, mostly leveraged longs, with Bitcoin alone accounting for around seven hundred fifty to seven hundred seventy million. Traders should care because the cascade flushed weak hands after a break of the two-hundred-day moving average and leaves the market testing key support with thin weekend liquidity.
items.impact: Heightened downside volatility and risk of further long flushes toward sixty thousand

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Post $1.91B Outflows Over Seven Sessions
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about one point nine one billion dollars in net outflows across seven straight sessions through November thirteenth, with Friday alone seeing one hundred eighty-five million in redemptions led by BlackRock's IBIT. This continues a broader multi-billion outflow stretch since late October. Institutional selling removes a key demand bid and signals risk-off among the funds that had previously driven much of the cycle's upside.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure and weaker institutional support into the new week

items.title: Anthropic Mega-IPO Seen Draining Crypto Liquidity
items.summary: Analysts and executives point to Anthropic's upcoming IPO, expected to price around November eighteenth and raise up to sixty-four billion dollars, as a major liquidity drain on Bitcoin. The pattern mirrors the roughly twenty percent drop ahead of the SpaceX listing earlier this year, with investors reportedly selling crypto to fund allocations amid heavy oversubscription. Traders should watch whether the selling eases after the listing, as history suggests a potential rebound once capital stops rotating out.
items.impact: Temporary capital rotation pressure with possible post-IPO relief bounce

items.title: Kava Lend Exploited for $3.8M; KAVA Crashes Nearly 40%
items.summary: An attacker drained roughly fifty-five million KAVA tokens worth about three point eight million dollars from Kava Lend by inflating collateral in a dormant BUSD market and borrowing repeatedly. Most of the tokens were bridged and sold on BNB Chain for around two point one million. KAVA plunged up to forty percent or more, with exchanges pausing withdrawals and transfers. This is a fresh DeFi security hit that can weigh on altcoin and lending-protocol sentiment while Bitcoin is already under pressure.
items.impact: Negative spillover to DeFi and altcoins; isolated but confidence-damaging

items.title: Crypto Fear and Greed Index Plunges to Extreme Fear at 10
items.summary: The Fear and Greed index dropped to ten, marking extreme fear as Bitcoin and the broader market sold off hard over the weekend. Total crypto market cap fell several percent into the low two-trillion range with only a handful of top coins green. Extreme readings like this often appear near capitulation points, so traders watch for stabilization or a bounce once leverage is fully flushed, though macro headwinds remain.
items.impact: Oversold conditions that can support a relief bounce if support holds

items.title: Bitcoin Briefly Rebounds as Shorts Get Squeezed After Flush
items.summary: After tagging the sixty-two thousand area, Bitcoin clawed back above sixty-five thousand at times on Sunday with bursts of short liquidations in the tens of millions. Some analysts called the move a rare leverage-driven flush and said they were buying the dip, citing stretched moving averages and historical parallels. Traders should note the bounce remains fragile ahead of Monday ETF flow data and unresolved macro catalysts like Fed expectations.
items.impact: Short-term relief possible but dependent on holding recent lows

items.title: US 10-Year Yield Tops 5.15% as Dollar Hits 19-Month High
items.summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to around 5.15 percent on Friday, marking its strongest weekly rise in over a year, while the dollar index reached about 103.4, its highest since April 2025. This came as markets fully priced a December Fed rate hike and raised odds of further tightening after hot inflation data. Crypto traders should care because higher yields and a stronger dollar tighten financial conditions, often pressuring risk assets like Bitcoin by raising the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets.
items.impact: Tighter conditions likely weigh on BTC and equities near-term

items.title: October PPI Rises 0.3% MoM, 6.5% YoY Highest Since 2022
items.summary: Producer prices increased 0.3 percent month-over-month in October, a touch below the 0.4 percent forecast, but the annual rate hit 6.5 percent, the biggest gain since late 2022. Core measures also showed persistent pressures, following a hotter-than-expected CPI earlier in the week. This keeps the Fed on a hawkish path and supports expectations for rate hikes, which matter for traders as it reinforces higher-for-longer rates that can dampen liquidity and risk appetite across markets including crypto.
items.impact: Reinforces Dec hike odds and broader tightening narrative

items.title: Fed's Jefferson: Inflation Trajectory Key for Policy Stance
items.summary: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said Friday that with the economy and labor market solid, the path of inflation is now the more important signal for determining the right monetary policy stance. He noted persistent price pressures in recent data and that further adjustments will depend on incoming numbers, the outlook, and risks. Traders should watch this because it signals the Fed remains focused on bringing inflation down, keeping the door open to additional hikes that could pressure Bitcoin through higher real rates.
items.impact: Supports hawkish Fed pricing into December meeting

items.title: Bessent vs Goolsbee Split on Energy Shock and Rate Hikes
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent argued Friday the Fed should not hike rates aggressively over an energy supply shock tied to the Iran conflict, calling the numbers noisy and urging a forward look. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee pushed back, saying inflation has broadened into services and beyond oil or tariffs, with AI-related demand also adding pressure. This debate highlights uncertainty around the inflation drivers heading into the December FOMC, important for crypto as it could sway the size and pace of any tightening and thus market liquidity.
items.impact: Adds uncertainty to December hike size and path

items.title: Retail Sales Due Tuesday; FOMC Minutes Wednesday
items.summary: No major US data prints today on Sunday, but Advance Retail Sales for October land Tuesday November 17 at 8:30 ET, followed by Industrial Production. FOMC minutes from the October hold meeting come out Wednesday at 2pm ET. These will give fresh reads on consumer spending strength and the Fed's internal debate after recent hot inflation, so traders need to position carefully as surprises could shift rate expectations and move Bitcoin sharply in either direction.
items.impact: Key catalysts that could reprice Fed path this week

items.title: Markets Price Near-Certain December Hike, Odds of 50bp Rise
items.summary: After the week's CPI and PPI data plus hawkish Fed comments, markets now price roughly 90 percent odds of a 25 basis point hike in December, with a 12 to 15 percent chance of a larger 50 basis point move, and further tightening into early 2027. Two-year yields jumped sharply on the week. For Bitcoin traders this elevates the discount rate on future cash flows and risk assets, often leading to de-risking until the path becomes clearer after the next data and the December meeting.
items.impact: Higher rate path pressures risk assets including crypto

items.title: Iran drones hit Bahrain base hosting US assets
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched drones at a US-linked radar and helicopter base in Bahrain early Sunday, the first major strike there in weeks. Bahrain says its defenses intercepted the attacks after sirens and explosions, while Tehran claims success and keeps the Strait of Hormuz closed. Traders should watch this closely because any Gulf escalation immediately lifts the oil risk premium and hits risk assets hard, especially with Hormuz shipping already disrupted.
items.impact: Higher oil prices and broader risk-off pressure on crypto and equities

items.title: Zelenskyy: US floated Donbas swap for NATO entry
items.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy revealed that American envoys asked whether Kyiv would pull out of remaining Donbas areas in exchange for NATO membership, the first time this land-for-security idea has been raised in talks. He stressed Ukraine will not recognize Russian control of territory but would put a full security package including guarantees and rebuild funds to a referendum if it materializes. This is a potential game-changer for ending the war; markets will price any credible de-escalation path as positive for risk assets while remaining skeptical until details firm up.
items.impact: Possible de-risking if talks advance, but unresolved for now

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin set historic APEC trilateral
items.summary: The White House confirmed the first-ever joint meeting of Trump, Xi Jinping and Putin on the sidelines of next week's APEC summit in Shenzhen, focused on nuclear arms control and the Iran war. Ukraine is deliberately off the agenda, and officials expect no major deals, just the start of talks among the three biggest nuclear powers. Crypto traders care because any signal of great-power coordination or friction on energy, nukes or trade can swing global risk sentiment and dollar flows overnight.
items.impact: High-uncertainty event risk with limited immediate directional bias

items.title: Saudi coalition downs Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted two ballistic missiles headed for Riyadh and several drones over the oil-rich Eastern Province on Sunday. Houthis have stepped up strikes on Saudi energy and capital targets in recent days, including prior hits near Aramco facilities. This keeps Gulf energy infrastructure under direct threat and supports elevated oil prices even as other supply factors ease, which feeds into inflation and risk-asset volatility.
items.impact: Sustains oil risk premium and energy-driven market jitters

items.title: Ukraine drones hit key Russian Astrakhan airfield
items.summary: Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Akhtubinsk military airfield in Russia's Astrakhan region overnight, with reports of at least 30 explosions, fires and secondary detonations at aircraft parking and ammo sites. The base hosts advanced flight testing and Su-34 bombers used against Ukraine, about 650 kilometers from the front. Deep strikes like this show the war's reach into Russian territory continues unabated, keeping geopolitical risk elevated without a clear peace catalyst.
items.impact: Maintains war-risk backdrop with limited new directional catalyst

items.title: Israel kills senior Hamas Oct 7 planner in Gaza
items.summary: Israel confirmed it killed Samir Abu Younis, the Rafah Brigade commander who helped plan and oversee the October 7 2023 attack, in a strike on a southern Gaza tent camp. Hamas acknowledged the death and called it an assassination; the strike comes amid a fragile longer-term ceasefire that has not stopped targeted operations. This keeps Middle East tensions simmering and can add to regional risk premium, though it is more localized than the Gulf or Ukraine fronts for global markets.
items.impact: Adds to ME volatility without major oil or systemic shock
